supply.heading: When the look is the brief

items.title: Height and stature
items.body: Performers at the far ends of the range — from very tall to very short — cast for roles written around their height, and represented as actors rather than as a measurement.

items.title: Twins and lookalikes
items.body: Identical and non-identical twins, close matches and doubles for continuity, split-screen, time-jump and multiple-role work.

items.title: Distinctive features
items.body: Faces and figures that stay with an audience — striking bone structure, natural hair, tattoos, scarring, and looks a standard casting call rarely reaches.

items.title: Character and real people
items.body: Faces with a life behind them, for productions and brands that want believable over polished, and memorable over neutral.

approach.heading: Performers first, description second
approach.body: Everyone on this roster is here as a professional performer. We cast them for what a brief actually needs, we ask before we describe anyone in a particular way, and we do not put people forward for work that trades on their appearance at their expense. If a role is written badly or a treatment is heading somewhere we would not be comfortable sending someone into, we will raise it with you early rather than quietly decline. It has never cost a good production anything to be asked.

points.description: Billed and briefed as performers, with the same credits, rates and conditions as any other booking.
How someone is described in a submission is agreed with them, not assumed by us or by a brief.
If a role is wrong for the person or the person is wrong for the role, you will hear it from us first.
